---
## [EN] Introduction & Naming (L'Épure)
URL: https://giskard-ai.github.io/epure/introduction

# Introduction & The Meaning of EPURE

**EPURE** (`Giskard-AI/epure`) is a GitHub-first, specification-driven software engineering framework that combines **structured human architectural governance** with **autonomous multi-agent TDD implementation and code review**.

**EPURE** brings a deterministic specification lock (`spec_sha`), a single declarative repository configuration (`.github/agents.yml`), and a reproducible issue-to-release workflow to AI-assisted software engineering.

---

## Why the Name "EPURE"?

The name **EPURE** carries a dual meaning rooted in French architectural heritage and modern software engineering:

### 1. The Architectural Blueprint (*L'Épure d'Architecte*)

In classical French architecture, stonecutting (*stéréotomie*), and naval carpentry, **une épure** is the full-scale geometrical working drawing traced on a workshop wall or floor before a single block of stone is cut or a beam is shaped.

In software engineering with AI agents, the most common failure mode is **premature coding**: letting an LLM guess product requirements, invent domain vocabulary, or silently choose trade-offs inside a pull request. EPURE enforces the exact opposite discipline:

1. **Draw the blueprint first**: On a GitHub tracking issue, the maintainer and the agent clarify every ambiguity through a structured interview (**Grill**).
2. **Version the domain and specification**: Before any application code is written, EPURE commits the ubiquitous language (`GLOSSARY.md`), Architectural Decision Records (`docs/adr/`), the functional & technical specification (`docs/specs/<slug>.md`), and—when a user interface is involved—the visual design contract (`DESIGN.md`) onto a dedicated `plan/<issue>-<slug>` branch.
3. **Machine the parts under a locked mandate**: Only after a human maintainer signs the blueprint with `/epure approve` (locking the exact `spec_sha` in `refs/epure/state/<issue>`) do agents execute the dependency-ordered ticket DAG (`task/* -> feature/*`).

### 2. The Bilingual Acronym

**EPURE** also stands for the four pillars of its execution engine:

| Letter | English Acronym | French Acronym | Engineering Role |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **E** | **Engineered** | **Élaboration** | Structured design interview (`/epure plan` & Grill) that surfaces trade-offs before coding. |
| **P** | **Planning** | **Plans** | Versioned `GLOSSARY.md`, ADRs, `DESIGN.md`, Specification, and dependency-ordered ticket DAG (`blocked_by`). |
| **U** | **Unified** | **Usinage** | Secretless TDD implementation loop (`npm test`, `npm run build`, contract checks) on isolated `task/*` branches. |
| **R** | **Review** | **Revue** | Multi-agent specialist code review loaded from trusted `dev`, Impeccable WCAG AA UI gate, and AI semantic squash. |
| **E** | **Execution** | **Exécution** | Governed integration (`feature/* -> dev` human merge) and fast-forward release promotion (`dev -> main`). |

---

## The Three-Tier Step Taxonomy (Q101)

A core principle of EPURE is transparency about **who decides** and **what runs automatically**. Every step in an EPURE workflow belongs to one of three formal categories:

<ArchifyDiagram
  slug="epure-issue-flow"
  locale="en"
  title="EPURE Global Issue & PR Flow (Human Gates, Mandatory & Conditional Steps)"
  caption="The complete EPURE workflow separated into Mandatory Human Gates, Mandatory Automated Pipeline, Conditional UI Gate, and Optional Controls."
/>

### 1. <span class="epure-badge epure-badge--human">Mandatory Human Validation Gates (4)</span>

No agent can ever bypass these four decision points. They require an explicit action from a repository contributor with `write` or `admin` permission:

1. **Gate 1 — Initiate & Answer the Grill (`/epure plan`)**: A maintainer triggers `/epure plan` on a GitHub Issue and answers the clarifying questions until the design frontier is settled.
2. **Gate 2 — Sign the Implementation Mandate (`/epure approve`)**: After reviewing the generated spec and ticket DAG on `plan/<issue>-<slug>`, a maintainer comments `/epure approve`. This merges `plan/* -> dev`, locks `spec_sha` in `refs/epure/state/<issue>`, and opens `feature/<issue>-<slug>`.
3. **Gate 3 — Human Integration Merge (`feature/* -> dev`)**: Once all tickets in the DAG are implemented, reviewed, and squashed into `feature/*`, EPURE opens the final synthesis PR `feature/* -> dev`. The `epure-dev-governance` ruleset **blocks** the Agent App from merging application code into `dev`: a human maintainer must click **Squash and merge**.
4. **Gate 4 — Human Release Promotion (`dev -> main`)**: Promoting `dev` to `main` and publishing a `vX.Y.Z` tag requires a human to trigger the `release-promote.yml` workflow (`workflow_dispatch`).

### 2. <span class="epure-badge epure-badge--auto">Mandatory Automated Steps</span>

Once a human gate is crossed, EPURE executes these steps deterministically on every feature:

- **Blueprint & Ticket DAG Generation**: Commits `GLOSSARY.md`, `docs/adr/`, and `docs/specs/<slug>.md` on `plan/<issue>-<slug>`, and creates GitHub Issues for each atomic task with `blocked_by` dependencies and the `ready-for-agent` label.
- **Secretless Sandbox TDD Loop**: For each unblocked ticket, implements tests and production code inside an isolated environment stripped of `LLM_API_KEY` and GitHub App private keys.
- **Trusted `dev` Multi-Agent Review & AI Semantic Squash**: Runs up to 4 domain-specialized reviewers (loaded strictly from `dev`) plus `spec-parity-reviewer`. On approval (`0 must_fix`), synthesizes a Conventional Commit title/body (`Refs #<ticket>`) and squash-merges `task/* -> feature/*`.
- **Final Synthesis PR Review**: Audits the consolidated diff on `feature/* -> dev` with `Closes #<issue>` and `Closes #<ticket>` trailer links.

### 3. <span class="epure-badge epure-badge--optional">Optional or Conditional Steps</span>

These steps run only when triggered by the nature of the change or by an explicit maintainer command:

- **Conditional UI & Impeccable Gate (automatic when UI exists)**: When the feature or diff touches frontend/UI files (`.vue`, `.tsx`, `.jsx`, `.css`, `.html`), EPURE automatically generates `DESIGN.md`, runs `user-advocate` in `design-gate` mode before `/epure approve`, and enforces `user-advocate` (`implementation-review`) + `impeccable-gate` as blocking checks on every PR. Pure backend/CLI changes skip these steps automatically.
- **Optional Exploratory Prototype (`/prototype` & Isolated Pages Preview)**: When a layout or state interaction cannot be settled in prose during the Grill, a maintainer can request a throwaway prototype on `prototype/*`. Static GitHub Pages preview is **disabled by default** (`enable_pages_preview: false`) and requires explicit opt-in.
- **Optional Granular Slash Commands**:
  - `/epure to-spec`: Force immediate transition from Grill to specification generation.
  - `/epure to-tickets`: Force ticket DAG creation from an existing specification.
  - `/epure status`: Refresh and post the current orchestration state and ticket table.
  - `/epure cancel`: Immediately halt orchestration and mark the mandate `cancelled` in `refs/epure/state/<issue>`.
- **Conditional Human Escalation (`needs-human`)**: Triggered automatically if a `task/*` branch touches sensitive paths (`.github/workflows/**`, `.cursor/agents/**`, `CODEOWNERS`) without an approved exception, or if a ticket still fails after `max_code_fix_attempts = 3` remediation rounds.

---

## [EN] Installation & /setup-repo Skill
URL: https://giskard-ai.github.io/epure/installation

# Installation & Bootstrap

The recommended way to initialize or reconfigure a repository with EPURE is to invoke the **`/setup-repo` agent skill** (`.agents/skills/setup-repo/SKILL.md`) directly inside your coding agent (Cursor, Claude Code, Pi, or Codex).

The `/setup-repo` skill orchestrates the entire bootstrap end-to-end: it inspects your repository's actual architecture, walks you through the interactive wizard (`setup-github-apps-wizard.sh`) to register your two GitHub Apps, runs the deterministic CLI (`dist/cli/setup-repo.mjs`) in `--dry-run` simulation mode before `--apply`, and **dynamically designs your multi-agent reviewer roster (`.cursor/agents/*.md`)**.

---

## System Requirements

Before bootstrapping a repository with EPURE, ensure your local environment has:

- **A Skills-compatible coding agent** (Cursor, Claude Code, Pi, or Codex) with `.agents/skills/setup-repo/SKILL.md`
- **Node.js 24 LTS** (`>=24.0.0`)
- **GitHub CLI (`gh`)** authenticated against your target GitHub account or organization (`gh auth status`)
- **Git** (`>=2.38`)
- **An LLM API Key** (`LLM_API_KEY` — defaults to Google Gemini `gemini-3.8-flash` with `thinking_level: HIGH`)

---

## Recommended Way: Bootstrap via the `/setup-repo` Skill

Open your target repository in your coding agent and invoke the **`/setup-repo`** skill:

```text
/setup-repo my-org/craft-calculator
```

The agent executes a guided **4-step workflow** with explicit human confirmation before any sensitive action:

### Step 1: Agent Inspection of Stack & Domain Elements

Before writing any file, the agent inspects the target repository (`package.json`, `pyproject.toml`, `Cargo.toml`, `go.mod`, `Makefile`, `src/` directory layout, UI presence, existing `GLOSSARY.md`) to determine:

- The language and build stack to configure `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, Renovate, and `standards-reviewer.md`.
- Whether the repository includes a frontend/UI surface (which determines whether the **Impeccable** gate and `frontend-reviewer`, `accessibility-reviewer`, and `design-reviewer` are included).
- Which domain subsystems warrant creating **custom specialist reviewers** in `.cursor/agents/<domain>-reviewer.md`.

### Step 2: Provision the Two GitHub Apps & 5 Secrets (Wizard)

To enforce strict privilege separation (Q82, Q91), EPURE never uses a single all-powerful Personal Access Token. Instead, every repository or organization uses **two distinct GitHub Apps**:

1. **Agent App (`<owner>-epure-agent`)**: Used by the orchestrator for day-to-day automation (`plan/*`, `task/*`, `feature/*`, Issues, PRs, and Check Runs). It is **never** a Bypass Actor on `dev` or `main`.
2. **Release App (`<owner>-epure-release`)**: Used exclusively by `release-promote.yml` when a human triggers a fast-forward release from `dev` to `main`. It is the **sole Bypass Actor** on `main` and `v*` tags.

If the apps are not yet registered, the `/setup-repo` skill launches the interactive wizard (which uses the GitHub App Manifest flow and stores secrets via `gh secret set` without ever exposing PEM private keys to the LLM):

```bash
bash scripts/wizards/setup-github-apps-wizard.sh --repo my-org/craft-calculator
```

| Secret Name | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `LLM_API_KEY` | API key for the LLM proxy sidecar (kept out of the code execution sandbox). |
| `EPURE_AGENT_APP_ID` | Numeric App ID of `<owner>-epure-agent`. |
| `EPURE_AGENT_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` | PEM private key of `<owner>-epure-agent` (used to mint short-lived installation tokens). |
| `EPURE_RELEASE_APP_ID` | Numeric App ID of `<owner>-epure-release`. |
| `EPURE_RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` | PEM private key of `<owner>-epure-release` (used only by `release-promote.yml`). |

### Step 3: Non-Destructive Simulation (`--dry-run`)

The `/setup-repo` skill first runs the underlying CLI in `--dry-run` mode and presents the complete file, branch, label, and ruleset plan for your approval:

```bash
node dist/cli/setup-repo.mjs \
  --repo my-org/craft-calculator \
  --target-dir /path/to/craft-calculator \
  --agent-app-id 123456 \
  --release-app-id 654321 \
  --dry-run
```

### Step 4: Guided Application (`--apply`) & Custom `.cursor/agents/` Design

Once you confirm the dry-run report, the `/setup-repo` skill applies the repository governance via `--apply --apply-github-settings`, and then creates and tailors the `.cursor/agents/*.md` reviewer prompts specific to your repository:

```bash
node dist/cli/setup-repo.mjs \
  --repo my-org/craft-calculator \
  --target-dir /path/to/craft-calculator \
  --agent-app-id 123456 \
  --release-app-id 654321 \
  --apply \
  --apply-github-settings
```

---

## What the `/setup-repo` Skill Configures

1. **Branch Topology (`main` & `dev`)**:
   - Ensures both `main` (immutable release line) and `dev` (active integration branch) exist.
   - Sets **`dev` as the default branch** of the repository so Pull Requests target `dev` by default and `Closes #<issue>` trailers resolve automatically when landing on `dev`.
2. **Canonical Triage Labels**:
   - Creates or updates the 5 canonical labels (`needs-triage`, `needs-info`, `ready-for-agent`, `ready-for-human`, `wontfix`) plus orchestration labels (`needs-human`, `approved-sensitive-change`).
3. **Declarative Configuration & Thin Caller Workflows**:
   - Generates `.github/agents.yml` pinned to the latest immutable 40-character commit SHA of `Giskard-AI/epure`.
   - Installs `.github/workflows/epure-issue-command.yml`, `.github/workflows/epure-check.yml`, `.github/workflows/pr-title.yml`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (tailored to the detected stack), and `.github/workflows/release.yml`.
4. **Dynamic Multi-Agent Reviewer Roster (`.cursor/agents/*.md`)**:
   - The agent running `/setup-repo` **creates, designs, and adds the appropriate `.cursor/agents/<role>-reviewer.md` files as needed** based on the repository's actual elements (further refined during `/epure plan`):
     - **Always-On Core (Cross-Cutting & Persona)**: `architecture-reviewer`, `security-reviewer`, `spec-parity-reviewer`, `standards-reviewer` (adapted to the detected language: TypeScript, Python, Rust, or Go), and `user-advocate`.
     - **Agent-Designed Stack, Domain & UI Specialists**: `domain-backend-reviewer`, `infra-reviewer`, any custom domain specialists designed by the agent for your subsystems (e.g. `realtime-reviewer.md`, `combat-engine-reviewer.md`, `sql-migration-reviewer.md` with YAML frontmatter `paths:` routing), and — only when the project includes a UI — the frontend/Impeccable trio (`frontend-reviewer`, `accessibility-reviewer`, `design-reviewer`).
     - *Illustrative example on `craft-calculator` (TypeScript + React web app)*: the agent composes a 10-reviewer roster combining the always-on core, `domain-backend-reviewer`, `infra-reviewer`, and the 3 UI/Impeccable reviewers.
5. **Squash-Only Merge Governance & 3 Repository Rulesets**:
   - Configures the repository to allow **Squash merge only** (`allow_squash_merge: true`, `allow_merge_commit: false`, `allow_rebase_merge: false`, `delete_branch_on_merge: true`).
   - Installs the 3 GitHub Repository Rulesets:
     - `epure-feature-governance` (`refs/heads/feature/*`): `Agent App` in PR bypass for autonomous `task/* -> feature/*` squash-merges once checks pass.
     - `epure-dev-governance` (`refs/heads/dev`): No `Agent App` bypass (`required_approving_review_count: 0` by default for solo-maintainer compatibility; configurable via `--require-pr-approvals <N>`).
     - `epure-release-immutability` (`refs/heads/main`, `refs/tags/v*`): `Release App` as sole Bypass Actor.

---
## [EN] Basic Usage (Case Study: craft-calculator)
URL: https://giskard-ai.github.io/epure/basic-usage

# Basic Usage (Real-World Case Study: `craft-calculator`)

To understand how EPURE works in practice, this guide walks through a complete, anonymized real-world feature lifecycle on a TypeScript/React web application called **`my-org/craft-calculator`** (a probability and cost optimizer for an incremental crafting system).

We will follow **Issue #16** from its initial 3-line description all the way to the **`v1.0.0`** production release on `main`.

---

## Visual State Machine of the Issue

Throughout this walkthrough, EPURE persists the orchestration state outside standard branches inside the atomic Git reference `refs/epure/state/16`:

<ArchifyDiagram
  slug="epure-state-machine"
  locale="en"
  title="EPURE Issue State Machine (CAS Git Ref: refs/epure/state/<issue>)"
  caption="Atomic Compare-And-Swap transitions in refs/epure/state/16 from Grilling to Completed."
/>

---

## Step 1: Open the Issue & Start the Grill

<span class="epure-badge epure-badge--human">Mandatory Human Gate 1</span>

A maintainer opens **Issue #16** (*"Add exact Markov-chain crafting simulator and responsive web dashboard"*) and posts a comment:

```text
/epure plan
```

### What EPURE Does Automatically

1. **Permission Gate**: Verifies that the commenter has `write` or `admin` access to `my-org/craft-calculator`.
2. **State Initialization**: Creates `refs/epure/state/16` in phase `grilling` and adds the `EPURE Status Dashboard` at the top of Issue #16.
3. **Structured Grill Round 1**: Inspects the repository and posts 4 targeted architectural questions on Issue #16:
   - *Q1: Should expected cost be computed via Monte Carlo simulation or exact absorbing Markov chains (`45 x 45` transition matrix)?*
   - *Q2: How should irreversible corruption states be modeled in the state space?*
   - *Q3: What is the persistence model for user price presets (backend DB vs. versioned `localStorage`)?*
   - *Q4: Does the web calculator require WCAG 2.1 AA contrast and mobile responsive layout (`320px`–`1440px`)?*

### Replying to the Grill (Implicit Continuity — Q84)

Because Issue #16 is in the `grilling` phase, **you do not need to type another slash command**. Simply reply in a normal GitHub comment:

```text
1. Exact absorbing Markov chain solver (Gaussian elimination, zero Monte Carlo variance).
2. Model corruption as an absorbing failure state that triggers item replacement cost.
3. Pure client-side SPA deployed on GitHub Pages with versioned localStorage.
4. Yes, enforce WCAG 2.1 AA and mobile-first responsive layout via Impeccable.
```

> **Batch Comment Cursor (`last_processed_comment_id`, Q75)**: If you post two or three follow-up comments in a row while the runner is queued, EPURE reads all unprocessed comments in strict chronological order on startup—no comment is ever lost.

---

## Step 2: Blueprint, `DESIGN.md`, Spec & Ticket DAG

<span class="epure-badge epure-badge--auto">Mandatory Automated Step</span> + <span class="epure-badge epure-badge--optional">Conditional UI Gate</span>

Once your reply settles all open questions on the design frontier, EPURE automatically transitions from **Grill** to **Blueprint & Tickets**:

1. **Creates branch `plan/16-markov-craft-calculator`** from `dev`.
2. **Commits the domain and specification artifacts**:
   - `GLOSSARY.md` (defining *Transition Matrix*, *Absorbing State*, *Expected Craft Cost*).
   - `docs/adr/0001-exact-markov-solver-and-spa.md`.
   - `DESIGN.md` (automatically generated because Issue #16 includes a UI surface, defining dark/light tokens, WCAG AA contrast, and responsive breakpoints).
   - `docs/specs/16-markov-craft-calculator.md` (complete specification enriched by `user-advocate` in **`design-gate`** mode with persona UX acceptance criteria).
3. **Creates the Dependency-Ordered Ticket DAG**:
   - **Issue #25**: *Core absorbing Markov solver & unit tests* (`ready-for-agent`, `blocked_by: []`)
   - **Issue #26**: *Preset price editor & versioned localStorage hook* (`ready-for-agent`, `blocked_by: [#25]`)
   - **Issue #27**: *Responsive simulator UI & Impeccable accessibility verification* (`ready-for-agent`, `blocked_by: [#25, #26]`)
4. **Opens PR `plan/16-markov-craft-calculator -> dev`** and pauses in state **`awaiting_approval`**.

---

## Step 3: Sign the Mandate (`/epure approve`)

<span class="epure-badge epure-badge--human">Mandatory Human Gate 2</span>

After reviewing the specification and ticket breakdown on the `plan/*` PR, the maintainer comments on Issue #16:

```text
/epure approve
```

### What `/epure approve` Locks In

- Squash-merges the documentation-only PR `plan/16-markov-craft-calculator -> dev`.
- Records the signed mandate in `refs/epure/state/16` (`spec_sha`, `approved_by`, `approved_at`, `status: "active"`).
- Creates the integration branch **`feature/16-markov-craft-calculator`** from `dev`.

---

## Step 4: Secretless TDD & Multi-Agent PR Reviews (`task/* -> feature/*`)

<span class="epure-badge epure-badge--auto">Mandatory Automated Step</span> + <span class="epure-badge epure-badge--optional">Conditional UI Gate</span>

EPURE now executes the ticket DAG in topological order (`#25`, then `#26`, then `#27`):

1. **Secretless Sandbox TDD**:
   - Creates `task/25-markov-solver` from `feature/16-markov-craft-calculator`.
   - Runs `npm test` and `npm run build` inside the isolated sandbox (`LLM_API_KEY` and GitHub App private keys are stripped from the child environment).
   - Opens **PR #28** (`task/25-markov-solver -> feature/16-markov-craft-calculator`).
2. **Independent Multi-Agent Review (from trusted `dev`)**:
   - Loads `.cursor/agents/*.md` strictly from `dev` (never from `task/25-*`).
   - Selects up to 4 relevant reviewers (e.g., `domain-backend-reviewer`, `standards-reviewer`, `security-reviewer`) plus `spec-parity-reviewer`.
   - For **Ticket #27** (which touches `.tsx` and `.css` files), automatically includes `frontend-reviewer`, `accessibility-reviewer`, `design-reviewer`, `user-advocate` (`implementation-review`), and the **`impeccable-gate`** check.
   - If a reviewer emits a `must_fix`, EPURE runs a targeted remediation round (up to `max_code_fix_attempts = 3`) and re-runs only the failed reviewers + `spec-parity-reviewer`.
3. **AI Semantic Squash Merge**:
   - Just before merging each `task/*` PR into `feature/16-markov-craft-calculator`, EPURE synthesizes a clean Conventional Commit title and body (`feat(solver): implement exact absorbing Markov chain solver (#28)` with `Refs #25`) and performs an autonomous squash-merge via the `epure-feature-governance` ruleset.

---

## Step 5: Final Synthesis PR & Human Merge into `dev`

<span class="epure-badge epure-badge--auto">Mandatory Automated Step</span> -> <span class="epure-badge epure-badge--human">Mandatory Human Gate 3</span>

Once tickets `#25`, `#26`, and `#27` are merged into `feature/16-markov-craft-calculator`:

1. EPURE opens the final synthesis **PR #47** (`feature/16-markov-craft-calculator -> dev`) with `Closes #16`, `Closes #25`, `Closes #26`, `Closes #27`.
2. Runs the full synthesis multi-agent review and `impeccable-gate` on the consolidated diff.
3. Updates the PR title and body with a synthesized Conventional Commit summary.
4. **Human Gate 3**: Because `epure-dev-governance` forbids the Agent App from merging code into `dev`, the human maintainer reviews PR #47 and clicks **Squash and merge**. GitHub automatically closes Issues `#16`, `#25`, `#26`, and `#27`.

---

## Step 6: Promote Release `dev -> main` (`v1.0.0`)

<span class="epure-badge epure-badge--human">Mandatory Human Gate 4</span>

When ready to cut a production release, the maintainer triggers the **`Release Promote (dev -> main)`** workflow (`workflow_dispatch` with `version: v1.0.0`), or runs via `gh`:

```bash
gh workflow run release-promote.yml -R my-org/craft-calculator -f version=v1.0.0
```

Using the isolated **Release App** (`<owner>-epure-release`), the workflow verifies that `main` is an ancestor of `dev`, performs an atomic fast-forward of `main` to `dev`, and pushes the immutable tag `v1.0.0`.

---
## [EN] Commands Reference (/epure & /setup-repo)
URL: https://giskard-ai.github.io/epure/commands

# Commands Reference (`/epure`, `/setup-repo` Skill & CLI)

EPURE is operated through two complementary surfaces:
1. **The local `/setup-repo` agent skill** (`.agents/skills/setup-repo/SKILL.md` — the **preferred way** to bootstrap or reconfigure a repository, its Rulesets, and its dynamic `.cursor/agents/*.md` reviewer roster).
2. **GitHub Issue slash commands (`/epure ...`)** to drive the feature lifecycle day-to-day directly from GitHub Issues.

---

## 1. GitHub Issue Slash Commands (`/epure`)

All `/epure` commands are posted as comments on a GitHub Issue. Every command is guarded by a **Fail-Closed Permission Gate**: the commenter must hold `write` or `admin` repository permissions.

| Command | Category (Q101) | Target Phase | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `/epure plan` | <span class="epure-badge epure-badge--human">Mandatory Human Gate 1</span> | `grilling` | Initializes `refs/epure/state/<issue>`, inspects the repository, and starts the structured architectural Grill interview. |
| *(Any human comment during Grill)* | <span class="epure-badge epure-badge--human">Mandatory Human Gate 1</span> | `grilling -> awaiting_approval` | Implicit Grill continuity (Q84): processes human answers via the batch cursor (`last_processed_comment_id`). Once all ambiguities are settled, automatically generates `plan/*` artifacts and the ticket DAG. |
| `/epure approve` | <span class="epure-badge epure-badge--human">Mandatory Human Gate 2</span> | `implementation` | Squash-merges the documentation-only `plan/* -> dev` PR, locks the signed `spec_sha` mandate in `refs/epure/state/<issue>`, opens `feature/<issue>-<slug>`, and executes the ticket DAG (`task/* -> feature/*`). Also supports **idempotent resumption** if re-run after an error. |
| `/epure to-spec` | <span class="epure-badge epure-badge--optional">Optional Override</span> | `spec` | Forces an immediate transition from the Grill to writing `GLOSSARY.md`, ADRs, `DESIGN.md`, and `docs/specs/<slug>.md` on `plan/*`. |
| `/epure to-tickets` | <span class="epure-badge epure-badge--optional">Optional Override</span> | `tickets` | Forces immediate decomposition of the specification on `plan/*` into a dependency-ordered GitHub Issue DAG (`blocked_by`). |
| `/epure status` | <span class="epure-badge epure-badge--optional">Optional Override</span> | *(Read-only)* | Reads `refs/epure/state/<issue>` and posts a fresh summary of the current phase, locked `spec_sha`, and per-ticket progress without mutating code. |
| `/epure cancel` | <span class="epure-badge epure-badge--optional">Optional Override</span> | `cancelled` | Marks the mandate as `cancelled` in `refs/epure/state/<issue>`, stops any new ticket execution, and preserves existing branches and audit logs. |

---

## 2. Repository Bootstrap Agent Skill (`/setup-repo` — Recommended)

The **`.agents/skills/setup-repo/SKILL.md`** skill is the **preferred way** to onboard or reconfigure an EPURE consumer repository from Cursor, Claude Code, Pi, or Codex:

```text
/setup-repo <owner>/<repo>
```

### What the `/setup-repo` Skill Does

1. **Project Discovery**: Inspects the repository stack (`package.json`, `pyproject.toml`, `Cargo.toml`, `go.mod`, `Makefile`), `src/` module layout, and whether a user interface is present.
2. **Dry-Run Simulation (`--dry-run`)**: Runs `dist/cli/setup-repo.mjs --dry-run` and presents the full plan to the human maintainer before writing anything.
3. **Dynamic `.cursor/agents/*.md` Roster Design**: Creates, designs, and tailors specialist reviewers according to the project's actual elements (always-on core `architecture-reviewer`, `security-reviewer`, `spec-parity-reviewer`, `standards-reviewer`, `user-advocate` + tailored domain/UI specialists with `paths:` routing).
4. **Idempotent Application (`--apply --apply-github-settings`)**: Writes `.github/agents.yml`, SHA-pinned caller workflows, configures squash-only merges, and provisions the 3 Repository Rulesets.

---

## 3. Underlying Bootstrap CLI (`dist/cli/setup-repo.mjs`)

Invoked automatically by the `/setup-repo` skill (or runnable directly from a terminal):

```bash
node dist/cli/setup-repo.mjs \
  --repo <owner>/<name> \
  --target-dir <path> \
  [--dry-run | --apply] \
  [--apply-github-settings] \
  [--no-frontend-reviewers] \
  [--domain-reviewers <slug1,slug2>] \
  [--agent-app-id <id>] \
  [--release-app-id <id>] \
  [--require-pr-approvals <N>]
```

| Flag | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--repo <owner/name>` | *(Required)* | Target GitHub repository slug (e.g., `my-org/craft-calculator`). |
| `--target-dir <path>` | Current directory | Local checkout path where `.github/agents.yml`, workflows, and `.cursor/agents/*.md` are written. |
| `--dry-run` | `true` (if `--apply` omitted) | Prints the complete bootstrap plan without modifying local files or calling write APIs. |
| `--apply` | `false` | Writes configuration files, caller workflows, and base `.cursor/agents/*.md` files. |
| `--apply-github-settings` | `false` | Applies squash-only repository settings and the 3 Repository Rulesets via the GitHub REST API. |
| `--no-frontend-reviewers` | `false` | Omits `frontend-reviewer`, `accessibility-reviewer`, and `design-reviewer` for headless repositories. |
| `--domain-reviewers <csv>` | None | Scaffolds additional `.cursor/agents/<slug>-reviewer.md` specialist files for domain subsystems. |
| `--agent-app-id <id>` | Optional | Numeric GitHub App ID of `<owner>-epure-agent` added as PR Bypass Actor on `epure-feature-governance` (`feature/*`). |
| `--release-app-id <id>` | Optional | Numeric GitHub App ID of `<owner>-epure-release` added as sole Bypass Actor on `epure-release-immutability` (`main` and `v*`). |
| `--require-pr-approvals <N>` | `0` | Number of human PR review approvals required on `dev` (`0` for solo-maintainer compatibility; `>=1` for teams). |

---

## 4. Interactive GitHub Apps Wizard (`setup-github-apps-wizard.sh`)

```bash
bash scripts/wizards/setup-github-apps-wizard.sh --repo <owner>/<name>
```

Guides a human maintainer through registering the two GitHub Apps (`<owner>-epure-agent` and `<owner>-epure-release`) via the GitHub App Manifest flow and uploading the 5 required repository secrets (`LLM_API_KEY`, `EPURE_AGENT_APP_ID`, `EPURE_AGENT_APP_PRIVATE_KEY`, `EPURE_RELEASE_APP_ID`, `EPURE_RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY`).

---
## [EN] Configuration (.github/agents.yml & renovate.json)
URL: https://giskard-ai.github.io/epure/configuration

# Configuration Reference (`.github/agents.yml`)

EPURE centralizes all orchestration, LLM, governance, and UI gate settings in a single versioned declarative file: **`.github/agents.yml`**.

---

## Complete Canonical Example

Below is a complete `.github/agents.yml` file with all supported keys and their defaults (Q78, Q91–Q96):

```yaml
# .github/agents.yml — Declarative EPURE Configuration
schema_version: 1

epure:
  # Immutable 40-character SHA of Giskard-AI/epure
  pinned_sha: "7f9f5aafa90acb68c5374cf00833881c0467cf67"

branches:
  # Active integration branch (set as the repository's default branch)
  default_integration: "dev"
  # Immutable production release branch (fast-forward only from dev)
  release: "main"

llm:
  provider: "google-gemini"
  # Primary reasoning & coding model
  model: "gemini-3.8-flash"
  thinking_level: "HIGH"
  # Lightweight zero-temperature model for AI semantic squash commit messages
  squash_summary_model: "gemini-3.8-flash"
  squash_summary_temperature: 0.0

orchestration:
  # Out-of-branch atomic CAS state prefix
  state_ref_prefix: "refs/epure/state/"
  # Maximum automated TDD / review remediation loops per ticket before escalating to needs-human
  max_code_fix_attempts: 3
  # Maximum parallel domain/transverse reviewers selected per PR diff (excluding spec-parity-reviewer)
  max_parallel_reviewers: 4
  # Enforce secretless sandbox execution (fails closed if secrets cannot be stripped)
  secretless_sandbox: true

review_roster:
  # Always load reviewer definitions from the trusted base branch (never from untrusted PR head)
  trusted_branch: "dev"
  directory: ".cursor/agents"
  # Mandatory reviewer on every PR
  always_include:
    - "spec-parity-reviewer"
  # Available specialist & transverse agents
  available:
    - "domain-backend-reviewer"
    - "frontend-reviewer"
    - "infra-reviewer"
    - "architecture-reviewer"
    - "security-reviewer"
    - "standards-reviewer"
    - "accessibility-reviewer"
    - "design-reviewer"
    - "user-advocate"

ui_governance:
  # Automatically activates DESIGN.md, user-advocate, and impeccable-gate when UI files are present
  impeccable_enabled: true
  design_system_path: "DESIGN.md"
  # Opt-in static GitHub Pages preview for /prototype branches (disabled by default, Q70)
  enable_pages_preview: false
  preview_retention_days: 14

sensitive_paths:
  # Modifying any of these paths on a task/* branch blocks auto-merge unless labeled approved-sensitive-change
  - ".github/workflows/**"
  - ".github/agents.yml"
  - ".cursor/agents/**"
  - "CODEOWNERS"
```

---

## Section-by-Section Reference

### `branches`

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `default_integration` | `string` | `"dev"` | Default branch of the repository where approved `plan/*` and human-reviewed `feature/*` PRs land. |
| `release` | `string` | `"main"` | Immutable release branch updated exclusively by `release-promote.yml` via fast-forward from `dev`. |

### `llm`

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `provider` | `string` | `"google-gemini"` | LLM provider managed by the runner-local proxy sidecar. |
| `model` | `string` | `"gemini-3.8-flash"` | Model used for Grill interviews, specification writing, TDD coding, and multi-agent reviews. |
| `thinking_level` | `"LOW" \| "MEDIUM" \| "HIGH"` | `"HIGH"` | Reasoning depth passed to Gemini `thinkingConfig`. |
| `squash_summary_temperature` | `number` | `0.0` | Deterministic temperature used to synthesize Conventional Commit titles and bodies before squash-merge (Q94). |

### `orchestration`

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `state_ref_prefix` | `string` | `"refs/epure/state/"` | Git reference namespace used for atomic Compare-And-Swap state persistence (Q76). |
| `max_code_fix_attempts` | `integer` | `3` | Maximum number of automated remediation rounds on a `task/*` or `feature/*` PR before adding `needs-human` and stopping (Q78). |
| `max_parallel_reviewers` | `integer` | `4` | Ceiling on domain/transverse reviewers selected per PR diff so review latency and signal-to-noise remain optimal (Q92). |
| `secretless_sandbox` | `boolean` | `true` | Strips `LLM_API_KEY` and GitHub App private keys from all child build/test processes; fails closed if isolation is unavailable (Q74). |

### `ui_governance`

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `impeccable_enabled` | `boolean` | `true` | Enables `DESIGN.md` generation, `user-advocate` (`design-gate` and `implementation-review`), and the blocking `impeccable-gate` CI check whenever UI files are touched (Q79, Q96). |
| `enable_pages_preview` | `boolean` | `false` | Opt-in flag to publish static `/prototype` previews to an isolated GitHub Pages environment (Q70, Q73). |
| `preview_retention_days` | `integer` | `14` | Number of days before hosted prototype previews are automatically purged (Q71). |

### `sensitive_paths`

Any modification to `.github/workflows/**`, `.github/agents.yml`, `.cursor/agents/**`, or `CODEOWNERS` on a `task/*` branch triggers a **Sensitive Path Escalation**: EPURE refuses autonomous merge into `feature/*` and applies the `needs-human` label unless a maintainer explicitly adds the `approved-sensitive-change` label (Q81, Q93).

---

## Supply-Chain & Renovate Security Policy (`renovate.json`)

Every EPURE repository (and `Giskard-AI/epure` itself) ships a hardened **`renovate.json`** generated by `/setup-repo` (Q46–Q48):

- **Quarantine Cooldown (No Day-1 Merges)**: Enforces `minimumReleaseAge: "3 days"` globally (`"7 days"` for minor updates and GitHub Actions/Docker images, `"14 days"` for major npm updates) coupled with `internalChecksFilter: "strict"` and `prCreation: "not-pending"` so newly published or compromised packages are quarantined before any PR is opened.
- **Maximum Safe Automation**: Groups minor, patch, pin, and digest updates into single weekly PRs (`npm-minor-and-patch`, `github-actions`, `docker`), pins exact versions (`rangeStrategy: "pin"`, `helpers:pinGitHubActionDigests`, `docker:pinDigests`), runs monthly `lockFileMaintenance`, and automatically rebases behind `dev` (`rebaseWhen: "behind-base-branch"`).
- **Post-Install Script Isolation**: Injects `npmrc: "ignore-scripts=true"` during Renovate lockfile resolution to prevent untrusted lifecycle scripts from executing.
- **No Unreviewed Auto-Merge into `dev`**: `automerge: false` and `platformAutomerge: false` are strictly enforced; Renovate PRs target `dev`, run the full CI + multi-agent review pipeline, and optionally trigger the assisted `auto_migrate` agent if a breaking change is detected on a verified Renovate App PR.

---
## [EN] Architecture, Security & Multi-Agent Review
URL: https://giskard-ai.github.io/epure/architecture

# Architecture, Security & Multi-Agent Review Model

EPURE is built from the ground up around **Defense-in-Depth**, **Least Privilege**, and **Out-of-Branch Deterministic State**. Every automation boundary is enforced both by GitHub Repository Rulesets and by local runtime sandboxing.

---

## 1. Security & Trust Boundaries Architecture

<ArchifyDiagram
  slug="epure-security-architecture"
  locale="en"
  title="EPURE Security & Trust Boundaries Architecture"
  caption="Interactive architecture diagram showing the Trusted Control Plane, Secretless Sandbox, Out-of-Branch CAS State, and Dual GitHub Apps."
/>

### Key Architectural Invariants

1. **Dual GitHub App Separation (`<owner>-epure-agent` vs. `<owner>-epure-release`, Q82 & Q91)**:
   - The **Agent App** mints short-lived RS256 installation tokens scoped to day-to-day orchestration (`plan/*`, `task/*`, `feature/*`). It is a Bypass Actor **only** on `epure-feature-governance` (`refs/heads/feature/*`), allowing autonomous integration of verified atomic tasks while physically blocking it from merging application code into `dev` or pushing to `main`.
   - The **Release App** is invoked exclusively by `release-promote.yml` under human `workflow_dispatch`. It is the sole Bypass Actor on `epure-release-immutability` (`refs/heads/main` and `refs/tags/v*`).
2. **Secretless Sandbox Execution (Q74)**:
   - When EPURE runs `npm test`, `npm run build`, or `pytest` on a `task/*` branch, the child process environment is scrubbed of `LLM_API_KEY`, `EPURE_AGENT_APP_PRIVATE_KEY`, and `EPURE_RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY`.
   - A malicious or compromised test script cannot exfiltrate credentials. If sandbox isolation fails, EPURE aborts **fail-closed**.
3. **Out-of-Branch CAS State (`refs/epure/state/<issue>`, Q76)**:
   - State transitions (`last_processed_comment_id`, signed `spec_sha`, retry counters, ticket status table) are stored as JSON blobs inside `refs/epure/state/<issue-number>` updated via atomic `git update-ref` Compare-And-Swap.
   - `dev` and `main` remain 100% free of machine-state commit noise.

---

## 2. Multi-Agent PR Review, Impeccable Gate & AI Squash Pipeline

<ArchifyDiagram
  slug="epure-review-pipeline"
  locale="en"
  title="EPURE Multi-Agent PR Review, Impeccable Gate & Semantic Squash Pipeline"
  caption="Trusted dev roster loading, read-only code inspection tools, Impeccable UI gate, and targeted remediation loop."
/>

### How the Review Pipeline Works (Q92–Q96)

1. **Trusted `dev` Roster Loading & Prompt-Injection Defense (OWASP LLM01)**:
   - Reviewer prompts (`.cursor/agents/*.md`) are **always** loaded from the trusted `dev` branch (with fallback to EPURE's embedded canonical templates), never from the untrusted `task/*` branch under review.
   - All PR diffs, commit messages, and issue comments are wrapped inside `<untrusted_pr_diff>` XML delimiters with explicit instructions to ignore any embedded prompt-override directives.
2. **Dynamic Selection (Up to 4 Specialists + `spec-parity-reviewer`)**:
   - Based on the files touched in the PR diff, EPURE selects up to 4 relevant reviewers from the roster (`domain-backend-reviewer`, `frontend-reviewer`, `infra-reviewer`, `architecture-reviewer`, `security-reviewer`, `standards-reviewer`, `accessibility-reviewer`, `design-reviewer`, `user-advocate`) alongside the mandatory `spec-parity-reviewer`.
3. **Read-Only Codebase Inspection Tools**:
   - Reviewers are not restricted to a narrow unified diff: they can invoke 4 read-only tools (`list_files`, `read_file`, `read_line_range`, `search_code`) to trace callers, types, and domain invariants across the repository.
4. **Targeted Auto-Remediation (`max_code_fix_attempts = 3`)**:
   - If any reviewer emits a `must_fix` item, EPURE runs a targeted code fix in the secretless sandbox and re-runs **only** the reviewers that failed in the previous round plus `spec-parity-reviewer`.
   - On `feature/* -> dev` synthesis PRs, any remediation is routed through a `task/review-fix-*` PR so `epure-feature-governance` is respected.
5. **AI Semantic Squash Synthesis (Q94)**:
   - Immediately before merging a validated PR, a zero-temperature call synthesizes a clean Conventional Commit title (`type(scope): summary (#PR)`) and bulleted body (`Refs #<ticket>` on `feature/*`, `Closes #<issue>` / `Closes #<ticket>` on `dev`).
6. **Integrated Upstream Quality & Audit Engines**:
   - **[Matt Pocock Agent Skills (`mattpocock/skills`)](https://github.com/mattpocock/skills)** — Specification-driven skills (`grill-with-docs`, `to-spec`, `to-tickets`, `tdd`, `code-review`) pinned in `skills-lock.json`.
   - **[Impeccable (`pbakaus/impeccable`)](https://github.com/pbakaus/impeccable)** — Design system (`DESIGN.md`) and WCAG 2.1 AA frontend quality gate (`actions/impeccable`).
   - **[iFixAi (`ifixai-ai/iFixAi`)](https://github.com/ifixai-ai/iFixAi)** — Deterministic authorization trajectory auditing (`actions/ifixai`).
   - **[Archify (`tt-a1i/archify`)](https://github.com/tt-a1i/archify)** — Showcase-validated interactive architecture diagrams (`scripts/archify/`).
   - **[zizmor (`woodruffw/zizmor`)](https://github.com/woodruffw/zizmor)** — GitHub Actions workflow static security analysis (`actions/zizmor-audit`).
   - **[Renovate (`renovatebot/renovate`)](https://github.com/renovatebot/renovate)** — Automated updates of SHA-pinned workflows and dependencies (`auto_migrate`).

---
## [EN] How-To: Onboard a Repository
URL: https://giskard-ai.github.io/epure/guides/how-to-onboard-repo

# How-To: Onboard a Repository with the `/setup-repo` Skill

This guide shows how to take a brand-new or existing GitHub repository (such as `my-org/craft-calculator`) and onboard it by invoking **the `/setup-repo` agent skill** (`.agents/skills/setup-repo/SKILL.md`)—the preferred way to configure EPURE's 2 GitHub Apps, 5 secrets, `.github/agents.yml`, dynamic `.cursor/agents/*.md` reviewer roster, and 3 Repository Rulesets.

---

## 1. Create the Two GitHub Apps & Repository Secrets

EPURE separates day-to-day agent privileges from production release privileges using two GitHub Apps:

- **`<owner>-epure-agent`**: Permissions `contents: write`, `issues: write`, `pull_requests: write`, `checks: write`.
- **`<owner>-epure-release`**: Permissions `contents: write`, `metadata: read`.

Run the interactive wizard (or let the `/setup-repo` skill prompt you to run it):

```bash
bash scripts/wizards/setup-github-apps-wizard.sh --repo my-org/craft-calculator
```

Verify that all 5 secrets are registered on your target repository:

```bash
gh secret list -R my-org/craft-calculator
```

Expected output:

```text
EPURE_AGENT_APP_ID
EPURE_AGENT_APP_PRIVATE_KEY
EPURE_RELEASE_APP_ID
EPURE_RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY
LLM_API_KEY
```

---

## 2. Invoke the `/setup-repo` Skill (Inspection & `--dry-run` Simulation)

Inside your coding agent (Cursor, Claude Code, Pi, or Codex), invoke the **`/setup-repo`** skill on the target repository:

```text
/setup-repo my-org/craft-calculator
```

The agent inspects the repository's elements (language, build scripts, UI presence, sub-domains in `src/`) and first runs the CLI in `--dry-run` mode:

```bash
node dist/cli/setup-repo.mjs \
  --repo my-org/craft-calculator \
  --target-dir /path/to/craft-calculator \
  --agent-app-id 123456 \
  --release-app-id 654321 \
  --dry-run
```

Check that the dry-run report presented by the agent lists:

- Creation of `.github/agents.yml` pinned to the 40-character SHA of `Giskard-AI/epure`.
- Creation of `.github/workflows/epure-issue-command.yml`, `epure-check.yml`, `pr-title.yml`, `ci.yml`, and `release.yml`.
- Dynamic initialization of the `.cursor/agents/*.md` reviewer roster designed by the agent for your stack and sub-domains (always-on core `architecture-reviewer`, `security-reviewer`, `spec-parity-reviewer`, `standards-reviewer`, `user-advocate` + tailored domain/UI specialists, yielding 10 agents for the `craft-calculator` web app example).
- Creation of the 3 Repository Rulesets (`epure-feature-governance`, `epure-dev-governance`, `epure-release-immutability`).

---

## 3. Confirm Application (`--apply`) & Commit to `dev`

Once you confirm, the `/setup-repo` skill runs `--apply --apply-github-settings` and tailors the `.cursor/agents/<role>-reviewer.md` definitions to your domain modules:

```bash
node dist/cli/setup-repo.mjs \
  --repo my-org/craft-calculator \
  --target-dir /path/to/craft-calculator \
  --agent-app-id 123456 \
  --release-app-id 654321 \
  --apply \
  --apply-github-settings
```

Then commit and push the generated files to `dev`:

```bash
cd /path/to/craft-calculator
git checkout dev
git add .github/ .cursor/agents/
git commit -m "chore(epure): bootstrap repository governance and workflows"
git push origin dev
```

---

## 4. Solo Maintainer vs. Team Mode (`--require-pr-approvals`)

- **Solo Maintainer (Default `--require-pr-approvals 0`)**: GitHub does not allow a user to approve their own Pull Request. Setting `required_approving_review_count: 0` on `epure-dev-governance` ensures you can click **Squash and merge** on `feature/* -> dev` PRs opened by EPURE while still blocking the `Agent App` from self-merging.
- **Multi-Maintainer Team (`--require-pr-approvals 1` or higher)**: Require at least one peer human approval in addition to green `verify-contract` and `ai-review` checks before merging into `dev`.

---
## [EN] How-To: Drive an Issue End-to-End
URL: https://giskard-ai.github.io/epure/guides/how-to-drive-an-issue

# How-To: Drive an Issue End-to-End

This guide provides a practical checklist for steering a feature or complex bugfix from an initial GitHub Issue to a ready-to-merge `feature/* -> dev` Pull Request, including optional overrides and failure recovery.

---

## 1. Launching the Plan (`/epure plan`)

1. Open a GitHub Issue describing the goal, user problem, or feature scope.
2. Post `/epure plan` in a comment.
3. Wait for the `epure-issue-command` workflow to post **Grill Round 1**.

### Tips for Answering the Grill

- **Reply in plain Markdown**: You do not need to prefix your answers with `/epure` while the issue is in phase `grilling`.
- **Multiple comments are safe**: Thanks to the batch cursor (`last_processed_comment_id`), if you add a second comment with an extra constraint while a run is queued, EPURE will process both comments in order.
- **Short-circuiting the Grill (Optional)**: If you feel the questions are already answered and want to jump straight to specification generation, comment `/epure to-spec`.

---

## 2. Reviewing the `plan/*` Pull Request

Once the Grill settles, EPURE opens a `plan/<issue>-<slug> -> dev` Pull Request and creates the ticket DAG. Before commenting `/epure approve`, check:

1. **`GLOSSARY.md`**: Are the new domain terms accurate and free of ambiguity?
2. **`docs/adr/`**: Do the Architectural Decision Records reflect your choices?
3. **`DESIGN.md` (if UI is involved)**: Are the color tokens, typography, and interaction states aligned with your product?
4. **`docs/specs/<slug>.md` & Ticket DAG**: Are the acceptance criteria and `blocked_by` relationships between tickets logical?

---

## 3. Approving & Monitoring Execution (`/epure approve` & `/epure status`)

Post `/epure approve` on the tracking issue.

- To inspect live progress at any time without opening the Actions tab, comment `/epure status` or check the **EPURE Status Dashboard** pinned at the top of the issue body.
- Inside the GitHub Actions run logs, expand the structured `::group::` sections to inspect:
  - Secretless TDD test/build output per ticket.
  - Read-only tool calls (`read_file`, `search_code`) made by each specialist reviewer.
  - Per-reviewer verdicts (`approved` vs. `changes_requested`).

---

## 4. Handling `needs-human` Escalations & Idempotent Resumption

EPURE pauses and applies the `needs-human` label in two situations:

1. **Sensitive Path Modification**: A `task/*` branch modified `.github/workflows/**`, `.github/agents.yml`, `.cursor/agents/**`, or `CODEOWNERS`.
   - *Resolution*: Inspect the diff. If legitimate, add the `approved-sensitive-change` label to the PR and comment `/epure approve` on the tracking issue.
2. **Remediation Cap Reached (`max_code_fix_attempts = 3`)**: A ticket failed tests or reviewer `must_fix` checks 3 times in a row.
   - *Resolution*: Push a manual fix commit to the `task/*` or `feature/*` branch (or clarify the spec), then comment `/epure approve` again on the tracking issue. EPURE's **idempotent resumption** automatically skips all already-closed tickets and resumes from the remaining work.

---
## [EN] How-To: Customize Reviewers & Impeccable Gate
URL: https://giskard-ai.github.io/epure/guides/how-to-customize-reviewers

# How-To: Customize the Multi-Agent Reviewer Roster & Impeccable Gate

When you invoke the **`/setup-repo`** skill (and subsequently during `/epure plan`), EPURE dynamically composes and adapts the reviewer roster in `.cursor/agents/*.md` along with the **[Impeccable (`pbakaus/impeccable`)](https://github.com/pbakaus/impeccable)** UI quality gate (`DESIGN.md` + `impeccable-gate`), building on the specification and review workflows from **[Matt Pocock's `mattpocock/skills`](https://github.com/mattpocock/skills)**. This guide explains how the roster is assembled for your project and how to tailor it while preserving prompt-injection immunity.

---

## 1. Always-On Core vs. Dynamic Specialists in `.cursor/agents/`

The roster generated by `/setup-repo` is not static: it combines an **always-on cross-cutting core** with **conditional specialists** tailored to your stack and sub-domains (such as the 10-agent example generated for the `craft-calculator` React web app, or custom specialists added via `--domain-reviewers realtime,game-systems` and `--no-frontend-reviewers` for headless repositories):

| Reviewer File | Category | Generation & Selection Condition |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `architecture-reviewer.md` | Always-On Cross-Cutting | Checks deep module boundaries, ADR compliance, and `GLOSSARY.md` ubiquity. |
| `security-reviewer.md` | Always-On Cross-Cutting | Audits secret hygiene, injection surfaces, and privilege boundaries. |
| `spec-parity-reviewer.md` | Always-On Cross-Cutting | Runs on **every** PR (`task/* -> feature/*` and `feature/* -> dev`) to verify 1-to-1 parity with the approved spec. |
| `standards-reviewer.md` | Always-On Cross-Cutting (Stack-Aware) | Adapted to the detected stack (TypeScript `it.each`, Python `pytest.mark.parametrize`, Rust, or Go). |
| `user-advocate.md` | Always-On Persona Gate | Operates in **`design-gate`** mode (on `plan/*` before `/epure approve`) and **`implementation-review`** mode (on PRs). |
| `domain-backend-reviewer.md` (`+ <domain>-reviewer.md`) | Dynamic Domain Specialist | Tailored to the repo's domain (and extendable via `--domain-reviewers <slug>`); selected when domain logic or APIs change. |
| `infra-reviewer.md` | Dynamic Infra Specialist | Selected when CI workflows, build scripts, or dependency manifests change. |
| `frontend-reviewer.md` | Conditional UI Specialist | Generated when the repo includes a UI; selected when `.vue`, `.tsx`, `.jsx`, or client state hooks are modified. |
| `accessibility-reviewer.md` | Conditional UI / Impeccable | Generated when the repo includes a UI; audits WCAG 2.1 AA contrast, semantic HTML, ARIA attributes, and `:focus-visible`. |
| `design-reviewer.md` | Conditional UI / Impeccable | Generated when the repo includes a UI; verifies adherence to `DESIGN.md` tokens, responsive layout, and interaction states. |

---

## 2. How the Agent Creates & Customizes Reviewer Prompts Safely

Because `.cursor/agents/**` is a **trusted sensitive path** (Q92):

1. **Tailored Reviewer Creation during `/setup-repo` (and manual additions on `dev`)**: During initial setup, the agent inspects your codebase and can design new specialist files in `.cursor/agents/<slug>-reviewer.md` with a `paths:` attribute in the YAML frontmatter (e.g., `paths: src/realtime, src/ws`). Whenever a PR touches a file matching `paths:` (or `<slug>`), `selectReviewersForDiff` automatically selects that specialist.
2. **Always commit changes to `dev`**: At runtime, the EPURE orchestrator loads `.cursor/agents/*.md` exclusively from the trusted `dev` branch—never from an unmerged `task/*` branch.
3. **Automatic Domain Enrichment during `/epure plan`**: When `/epure plan` runs on a new feature, EPURE enriches the domain reviewers and `.cursor/agents/user-advocate.md` on the `plan/<issue>-<slug>` branch with new domain invariants and personas. When you run `/epure approve`, those updates merge into `dev` before any `task/*` ticket starts.

---

## 3. Dogfooding & Customizing `DESIGN.md` (Impeccable Gate)

Whenever a repository or PR includes frontend files (`.vue`, `.tsx`, `.jsx`, `.css`, `.html`), the **`impeccable-gate`** check (`evaluateImpeccableFrontendPr`) validates the diff against `DESIGN.md`.

### Blocking vs. Non-Blocking Findings

`impeccable-gate` blocks a PR **only** on objective, verifiable violations:

- **Accessibility (`accessibility`)**: Missing `title` on `<iframe>`, missing `aria-label` on icon/action buttons, missing `:focus-visible` keyboard focus styles, or WCAG 2.1 AA contrast below `4.5:1`.
- **Layout & Responsive (`layout_overflow`)**: Unbounded horizontal overflow or broken mobile viewports (`320px`–`1440px`).
- **Design Tokens (`design_tokens`)**: Hardcoded arbitrary colors bypassing the CSS custom properties declared in `DESIGN.md`.
- **Interaction States (`interaction_states`)**: Interactive async components missing explicit `loading`, `ready`, or `error` states.

Subjective stylistic preferences never block a PR.

---
## [EN] How-To: Promote a Release (dev -> main)
URL: https://giskard-ai.github.io/epure/guides/how-to-release

# How-To: Promote a Release (`dev -> main`)

In EPURE, `dev` is the active default integration branch and `main` is the **immutable release line** protected by the `epure-release-immutability` ruleset. Neither developers nor the `Agent App` can push directly to `main`.

Promoting a release is the **4th Mandatory Human Validation Gate** (Q101).

---

## 1. Prerequisites Before Promoting

Before triggering a release promotion, verify that:

1. All target `feature/* -> dev` Pull Requests have been squash-merged into `dev`.
2. The `CI` workflow on the latest `dev` commit is green.
3. The repository secrets `EPURE_RELEASE_APP_ID` and `EPURE_RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` are configured, and `<owner>-epure-release` is listed as the Bypass Actor on `epure-release-immutability`.

---

## 2. Trigger the Release Promotion Workflow

You can trigger the release either from the GitHub web UI (**Actions** -> **Release Promote (dev -> main)** -> **Run workflow**) or via the `gh` CLI:

```bash
gh workflow run release-promote.yml \
  -R my-org/craft-calculator \
  -f version=v1.0.0
```

---

## 3. What `release-promote.yml` Executes

1. **Mints a Short-Lived Release App Token**: Signs an RS256 JWT using `EPURE_RELEASE_APP_ID` and `EPURE_RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` to obtain a short-lived installation token for `<owner>-epure-release`.
2. **Verifies Fast-Forward Ancestry**: Checks that `main` is a strict ancestor of `dev` (`git merge-base --is-ancestor origin/main origin/dev`). If `main` has diverged, the workflow aborts immediately without forcing a push.
3. **Atomic Fast-Forward & Tag**:
   - Pushes `dev` to `refs/heads/main` (`git push origin dev:refs/heads/main`).
   - Creates and pushes the annotated tag `v1.0.0` pointing to the exact promoted SHA.
   - Publishes the GitHub Release notes generated from the Conventional Commits merged since the previous tag.
4. **Revokes the Ephemeral Token**: Immediately revokes the installation token in an `always()` cleanup step.

---
## [EN] Domain Glossary (EN / FR)
URL: https://giskard-ai.github.io/epure/reference/glossary

# Domain Glossary (English / French Ubiquitous Language)

In accordance with **Q102**, the root `/GLOSSARY.md` file is the single canonical source of truth for EPURE's domain model (rendered natively in the [French Glossary](/fr/reference/glossary)).

This page provides the aligned **English <-> French** ubiquitous language reference table across all architectural rounds (Q1–Q103).

---

## 1. Workflow Step Taxonomy (Q101)

| English Term | French Canonical Term (`GLOSSARY.md`) | Definition & Invariant |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Mandatory Human Validation Gates (4)** | *Portes de validation humaine obligatoires (4 jalons)* | The 4 decision points that require an explicit action from a `write+` human contributor and can never be delegated to an agent: (1) `/epure plan` & Grill replies, (2) `/epure approve` locking `spec_sha`, (3) Human squash-merge of `feature/* -> dev`, and (4) Human `workflow_dispatch` of `release-promote.yml`. |
| **Mandatory Automated Steps** | *Étapes automatisées obligatoires* | Deterministic pipeline executed on every approved feature: `plan/*` artifact & ticket DAG generation, secretless TDD loop on `task/*`, multi-agent review from `dev` + AI semantic squash (`task/* -> feature/*`), and synthesis review on `feature/* -> dev`. |
| **Optional or Conditional Steps** | *Étapes facultatives ou conditionnelles* | Steps triggered either conditionally by the change surface (`DESIGN.md` + `user-advocate` + `impeccable-gate` when UI files exist; `needs-human` escalation on sensitive paths or `>3` fix attempts) or optionally by human command (`/prototype`, isolated Pages preview, `/epure to-spec`, `/epure to-tickets`, `/epure status`, `/epure cancel`). |

---

## 2. Core Orchestration & Branch Topology (Q1–Q85)

| English Term | French Canonical Term (`GLOSSARY.md`) | Definition & Invariant |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Tracking Issue (Orchestration Issue)** | *Issue de pilotage* | The GitHub Issue where `/epure plan` is invoked, hosting the Grill conversation, the status dashboard, and the `/epure approve` mandate. |
| **Plan Branch (`plan/<issue>-<slug>`)** | *Branche de plan (`plan/*`)* | Documentation-only branch holding `GLOSSARY.md`, ADRs, `DESIGN.md`, and `docs/specs/<slug>.md` before `/epure approve` merges it into `dev`. |
| **Feature Integration Branch (`feature/<issue>-<slug>`)** | *Branche d'intégration de fonctionnalité (`feature/*`)* | Branch created from `dev` upon `/epure approve` that receives autonomous squash-merges from `task/*` PRs before the final human merge into `dev`. |
| **Atomic Task Branch (`task/<ticket>-<slug>`)** | *Branche de tâche (`task/*`)* | Short-lived branch implementing a single ticket from the DAG in a secretless TDD sandbox. |
| **Out-of-Branch CAS State Ref (`refs/epure/state/<issue>`)** | *Référence Git d'état d'orchestration (`refs/epure/state/<issue-number>`)* | Dedicated Git reference outside `refs/heads/*` storing the state machine (`last_processed_comment_id`, signed `spec_sha`, retry counters) updated via atomic Compare-And-Swap. |
| **Batch Comment Cursor (`last_processed_comment_id`)** | *Traitement en lot des commentaires avec curseur* | Mechanism reading all unprocessed human comments in chronological order so queued runs never drop events. |
| **Implicit Grill Continuity** | *Continuité implicite de l'entretien de grill* | Automatic processing of any ordinary human comment posted while the issue is in phase `grilling`, without repeating a slash command. |

---

## 3. Security, Governance & Multi-Agent Review (Q86–Q103)

| English Term | French Canonical Term (`GLOSSARY.md`) | Definition & Invariant |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Secretless Sandbox & LLM Proxy** | *Proxy LLM de sandbox* | Isolation boundary stripping `LLM_API_KEY` and GitHub App private keys from consumer test/build subprocesses; fails closed if isolation is unavailable. |
| **Three Governance Rulesets (`epure-feature-governance`, `epure-dev-governance`, `epure-release-immutability`)** | *Séparation des trois Rulesets de gouvernance* | Three distinct GitHub Repository Rulesets: `Agent App` bypasses PRs only on `feature/*`; `dev` requires human merge (`0` review approvals by default for solo maintainer compatibility); `main` and `v*` allow only `Release App`. |
| **Trusted `dev` Reviewer Roster (`.cursor/agents/*`)** | *Roster de reviewers spécialisés et transverses* | Read-only reviewer definitions initialized by `setup-repo`, always loaded at runtime from `dev` (never from `task/*`), capped at 4 specialists per diff + `spec-parity-reviewer`. |
| **Persona UX Gate (`user-advocate`)** | *Porte UX orientée personas (`user-advocate`)* | Specialist evaluating end-user journeys in `design-gate` mode (enriching ticket acceptance criteria before `/epure approve`) and `implementation-review` mode (blocking PR check on UI changes). |
| **Blocking Design Violation (`impeccable-gate`)** | *Violation de design bloquante* | Objective new UI regression (WCAG 2.1 AA contrast, layout overflow, missing `DESIGN.md` tokens, or missing `loading`/`ready`/`error` interaction states) that blocks PR merge. |
| **AI Semantic Squash Synthesis** | *Synthèse de message de squash sémantique par IA* | Zero-temperature generation of a Conventional Commit title and body right before squash-merge (`Refs #<ticket>` on `feature/*`, `Closes #<issue>` on `dev`). |

---
## [FR] Introduction & Nom (L'Épure)
URL: https://giskard-ai.github.io/epure/fr/introduction

# Introduction & Sens du Nom EPURE

**EPURE** (`Giskard-AI/epure`) est un framework d'ingénierie logicielle centré sur GitHub qui associe **une gouvernance architecturale humaine structurée** à **une implémentation TDD et une revue de code multi-agents autonomes**.

**EPURE** garantit à l'ingénierie assistée par IA un verrouillage cryptographique du mandat de spécification (`spec_sha`), un fichier de configuration déclaratif unique (`.github/agents.yml`) et un flux reproductible de l'issue jusqu'à la release.

---

## Pourquoi le nom « EPURE » ?

Le nom **EPURE** possède un double sens qui ancre le projet à la fois dans la tradition architecturale française et dans l'ingénierie logicielle moderne :

### 1. L'Épure d'Architecte (Le Tracé Avant l'Usinage)

En architecture classique, en taille de pierre (*stéréotomie*) et en charpente navale, **une épure** est le dessin géométrique tracé à l'échelle grandeur nature sur le mur ou le sol de l'atelier avant même de tailler la première pierre ou d'assembler la moindre pièce.

Dans le développement logiciel assisté par agents IA, la cause principale d'échec est **le codage prématuré** : laisser un modèle deviner les besoins produit, inventer son propre vocabulaire métier ou trancher silencieusement des compromis d'architecture au milieu d'une Pull Request. EPURE impose la discipline inverse :

1. **Tracer l'épure d'abord** : sur une issue GitHub de pilotage, le mainteneur humain et l'agent lèvent chaque ambiguïté lors d'un entretien contradictoire structuré (**le Grill**).
2. **Versionner le domaine et la spécification** : avant qu'une seule ligne de code applicatif ne soit écrite, EPURE versionne le langage ubiquitaire (`GLOSSARY.md`), les décisions d'architecture (`docs/adr/`), la spécification fonctionnelle et technique (`docs/specs/<slug>.md`) et — dès qu'une interface utilisateur est concernée — le contrat de système de design (`DESIGN.md`) sur une branche dédiée `plan/<issue>-<slug>`.
3. **Usiner les pièces sous mandat verrouillé** : ce n'est qu'après la signature explicite du plan par un mainteneur via `/epure approve` (qui verrouille le `spec_sha` exact dans `refs/epure/state/<issue>`) que les agents exécutent le graphe orienté acyclique (DAG) de tickets (`task/* -> feature/*`).

### 2. Le Rétro-Acronyme Bilingue

**EPURE** résume également les cinq piliers de son moteur d'orchestration en français comme en anglais :

| Lettre | Acronyme Français | Acronyme Anglais | Rôle dans le cycle d'ingénierie |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **E** | **Élaboration** | **Engineered** | Entretien de conception structuré (`/epure plan` & Grill) qui explicite les compromis avant de coder. |
| **P** | **Plans** | **Planning** | Versionnement de `GLOSSARY.md`, des ADRs, de `DESIGN.md`, de la Spécification et du DAG de tickets (`blocked_by`). |
| **U** | **Usinage** | **Unified** | Boucle d'implémentation TDD en sandbox sans secret (`npm test`, `npm run build`, contrats) sur des branches `task/*` isolées. |
| **R** | **Revue** | **Review** | Revue de code multi-agents spécialisés chargés depuis `dev`, porte UI Impeccable WCAG AA et squash sémantique par IA. |
| **E** | **Exécution** | **Execution** | Intégration gouvernée (merge humain `feature/* -> dev`) et promotion de release fast-forward (`dev -> main`). |

---

## La Tripartition des Étapes du Flux (Q101)

Un principe fondateur d'EPURE est la clarté absolue sur **qui décide** et **ce qui s'exécute automatiquement**. Chaque étape du cycle de vie appartient à l'une des trois catégories formelles suivantes :

<ArchifyDiagram
  slug="epure-issue-flow"
  locale="fr"
  title="Flux Global d'une Issue & PR EPURE (Portes Humaines, Obligatoire & Conditionnel)"
  caption="Le flux complet d'EPURE réparti entre les 4 Portes Humaines Obligatoires, le Pipeline Automatisé Obligatoire, la Porte UI Conditionnelle et les Contrôles Facultatifs."
/>

### 1. <span class="epure-badge epure-badge--human">Portes de Validation Humaine Obligatoires (4 Jalons)</span>

Aucun agent ne peut contourner ces quatre points de décision. Ils exigent l'intervention explicite d'un contributeur disposant des droits `write` ou `admin` sur le dépôt :

1. **Jalon 1 — Lancement & Réponses au Grill (`/epure plan`)** : un mainteneur déclenche `/epure plan` sur une issue GitHub et répond aux questions de cadrage jusqu'à ce que toutes les ambiguïtés soient levées.
2. **Jalon 2 — Signature du Mandat d'Implémentation (`/epure approve`)** : après relecture de la spécification et du DAG de tickets générés sur `plan/<issue>-<slug>`, le mainteneur poste `/epure approve`. Cette commande fusionne `plan/* -> dev`, scelle le `spec_sha` dans `refs/epure/state/<issue>` et ouvre la branche d'intégration `feature/<issue>-<slug>`.
3. **Jalon 3 — Merge Humain d'Intégration (`feature/* -> dev`)** : lorsque tous les tickets du DAG sont implémentés, audités et squashés dans `feature/*`, EPURE ouvre la PR finale de synthèse `feature/* -> dev`. Le ruleset `epure-dev-governance` **interdit** matériellement à l'Agent App de fusionner du code applicatif dans `dev` : un humain doit cliquer sur **Squash and merge**.
4. **Jalon 4 — Promotion Humaine de Release (`dev -> main`)** : la promotion de `dev` vers `main` et la publication du tag `vX.Y.Z` exigent le déclenchement manuel (`workflow_dispatch`) du workflow `release-promote.yml` par un mainteneur.

### 2. <span class="epure-badge epure-badge--auto">Étapes Automatisées Obligatoires</span>

Dès qu'un jalon humain est franchi, l'orchestrateur EPURE exécute de manière déterministe :

- **Génération de l'Épure & du DAG de Tickets** : commit de `GLOSSARY.md`, `docs/adr/` et `docs/specs/<slug>.md` sur `plan/<issue>-<slug>`, puis création des issues GitHub atomiques avec leurs dépendances `blocked_by` et le label `ready-for-agent`.
- **Boucle TDD en Sandbox Sans Secret** : pour chaque ticket débloqué, écriture des tests et du code dans un environnement isolé dépourvu de `LLM_API_KEY` et des clés privées PEM des GitHub Apps.
- **Revue Multi-Agents depuis `dev` & Squash Sémantique IA** : exécution parallèle de jusqu'à 4 reviewers spécialisés (chargés exclusivement depuis la branche de confiance `dev`) + `spec-parity-reviewer`. En cas de succès (`0 must_fix`), synthèse d'un titre et corps Conventional Commit (`Refs #<ticket>`) et squash-merge automatique `task/* -> feature/*`.
- **Revue de Synthèse Finale** : audit complet du diff consolidé sur la PR `feature/* -> dev` avec génération des liens de fermeture `Closes #<issue>` et `Closes #<ticket>`.

### 3. <span class="epure-badge epure-badge--optional">Étapes Facultatives ou Conditionnelles</span>

Ces opérations ne s'activent que selon la nature du changement ou sur demande explicite d'un mainteneur :

- **Porte Conditionnelle UI & Impeccable (automatique si surface UI)** : dès que la fonctionnalité ou le diff touche des fichiers d'interface (`.vue`, `.tsx`, `.jsx`, `.css`, `.html`), EPURE génère automatiquement `DESIGN.md`, exécute `user-advocate` en mode `design-gate` avant `/epure approve`, puis impose `user-advocate` (`implementation-review`) et `impeccable-gate` comme checks bloquants sur chaque PR. Les projets ou tickets purement backend/CLI ignorent automatiquement cette étape.
- **Détour Exploratoire `/prototype` & Preview Pages Isolée (facultatif)** : lorsqu'un comportement visuel ou une machine d'état ne peut être tranché par le texte pendant le Grill, un mainteneur peut demander un prototype jetable sur `prototype/*`. La prévisualisation statique GitHub Pages est **désactivée par défaut** (`enable_pages_preview: false`) et nécessite un consentement explicite.
- **Commandes Slash de Pilotage Granulaire (facultatives)** :
  - `/epure to-spec` : force le passage immédiat du Grill à la rédaction de la spécification.
  - `/epure to-tickets` : force la génération immédiate du DAG de tickets à partir de la spec existante.
  - `/epure status` : rafraîchit et affiche l'état d'orchestration et la table d'avancement des tickets.
  - `/epure cancel` : interrompt immédiatement l'orchestration et marque le mandat `cancelled` dans `refs/epure/state/<issue>`.
- **Escalade Humaine Conditionnelle (`needs-human`)** : déclenchée automatiquement si une branche `task/*` modifie un chemin sensible (`.github/workflows/**`, `.cursor/agents/**`, `CODEOWNERS`) sans exception approuvée, ou si un ticket échoue encore après `max_code_fix_attempts = 3` tours d'auto-remédiation.

---

## Écosystème Amont & Crédits (ADR-0018)

EPURE s'appuie sur des dépôts open source, des skills d'agents, des outils de design et des moteurs de sécurité épinglés par révision (attributions complètes dans [`NOTICE`](https://github.com/Giskard-AI/epure/blob/dev/NOTICE) et [`skills-lock.json`](https://github.com/Giskard-AI/epure/blob/dev/skills-lock.json)) :

| Dépôt Amont | Licence | Rôle dans EPURE |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **[Matt Pocock Agent Skills (`mattpocock/skills`)](https://github.com/mattpocock/skills)** | MIT | Socle des skills de cadrage et d'exécution (`grill-with-docs`, `to-spec`, `to-tickets`, `domain-modeling`, `tdd`, `code-review`, `prototype`, `wizard`, `pr` avec crédit à [Dex Horthy / HumanLayer](https://github.com/humanlayer/humanlayer)). |
| **[Impeccable (`pbakaus/impeccable`)](https://github.com/pbakaus/impeccable)** | Apache-2.0 | Cadrage UX/UI (`shape`, `DESIGN.md`, `.impeccable/surfaces/*.md`) et contrôle qualité déterministe frontend / accessibilité WCAG 2.1 AA (`actions/impeccable`, `impeccable-gate`). |
| **[Archify (`tt-a1i/archify`)](https://github.com/tt-a1i/archify)** | MIT | Moteur de schémas d'architecture interactifs en qualité showcase embarqué dans `scripts/archify/` (`npm run docs:diagrams`). |
| **[iFixAi (`ifixai-ai/iFixAi`)](https://github.com/ifixai-ai/iFixAi)** | Apache-2.0 | Audit déterministe des trajectoires d'autorisation et des frontières de privilèges (`actions/ifixai`). |
| **[zizmor (`woodruffw/zizmor`)](https://github.com/woodruffw/zizmor)** | MIT | Analyse statique de sécurité des workflows GitHub Actions (`actions/zizmor-audit`). |
| **[Renovate (`renovatebot/renovate`)](https://github.com/renovatebot/renovate)** | AGPL-3.0 (Outil) | Mise à jour automatisée des workflows épinglés par SHA et des dépendances avec migration assistée optionnelle (`auto_migrate`). |
